messages:
marta: heads up — ran a cost audit and saw a 38% bump in GPU spend last 24h in us-west1. most of it is from spot pools, but surprisingly autoscaler didn't reclaim a bunch of small idle pods. logging shows many nodes stuck in Terminating for >10m after preempt notice. any quick wins before we break out the big refactor?

sahil: :eyes: do you have the termination notice handler logs? sounds like the drain hook isn't completing or kube-proxy is blocking finalizers.

marta: pasted snippets from node agent below, truncated. looks like preempt hook runs but kubelet never evicts 'gpu-work' pods — they keep Restarting and keep PV mounts.

```
2026-03-18T02:14:04Z node-agent INFO received termination_notice (spot)
2026-03-18T02:14:05Z node-agent INFO starting graceful-drain ttl=120s
2026-03-18T02:15:30Z kubelet WARN Pod gpu-work still has finalizer "external-storage/detach"
2026-03-18T02:24:12Z node-agent ERROR drain timed out, re-queueing fallback
```

kevin: that finalizer is a clue. storage detach can block node drain > eviction TTL. we should not rely on a single short TTL for GPUs; 120s is too short for PV-backed jobs.

olivia: +1. also the autoscaler’s scale-down-safety is probably prevented by PDBs on those jobs. are these batch jobs using PDBs?

marta: some are using PDBs to avoid chaos. but these are low-priority batch training jobs — we can tolerate interruption if we checkpoint. they have an in-house sidecar that checkpoints, but the sidecar sometimes fails to upload before node is gone.

sahil: quick mitigation plan:
- increase termination hook TTL to 5m for spot GPU pools (buy time for checkpoint uploads)
- run a preempt-prober daemonset to proactively mark pods as lower-priority and trigger checkpoint earlier
- add a short-lived annotation to bypass storage finalizer on known checkpointed jobs (careful with data integrity)

ryan: we should also change autoscaler expander to "least-waste" and tune scale-down-unneeded-time to avoid killing nodes with expensive GPU warmup. current aggressive scale-down might be thrashing between spot and ondemand.

kevin: example autoscaler patch:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: ClusterAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleDown:
    enabled: true
    unneededTime: 10m
  expander: "least-waste"
```

olivia: another pattern that helped us elsewhere: eviction-staircase. Instead of draining the whole node immediately, run a staged eviction: first cordon + evict non-GPU-critical pods, then after a short wait evict batch jobs if they have confirmed checkpoint. This reduces blocked finalizers affecting everything on the node.

marta: sounds promising. can you sketch a node-lifecycle hook script we can drop into DaemonSet?

sahil: here's a small sketch — it listens for termination notice, cordons node, evicts non-gpu pods, signals sidecars to checkpoint, waits, then evicts gpu pods. uses kubectl for simplicity:

```
#!/bin/bash
NODE="$HOSTNAME"
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=$NODE -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["gpu-critical"]!="true") | .metadata.name' | xargs -r -n1 kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30
# signal sidecars
kubectl label node $NODE preempting=true
sleep 180
# evict gpu jobs after checkpoint window
kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=$NODE -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["gpu-critical"]=="true") | .metadata.name' | xargs -r kubectl delete pod --grace-period=60
```

kevin: +1 but prefer eviction API with eviction subresource; use retries. also add annotation on pods that confirms checkpoint completed so we don't evict in-flight ones.

olivia: for long-term: mixed-capacity pool improvements — tag cheaper spot pools with lower eviction-priority (taint: spot=fair-share:NoSchedule) and set critical services with tolerations only for on-demand pools. that way autoscaler will avoid mixing critical replicas onto spot nodes.

marta: example toleration for critical service:
```
tolerations:
- key: "spot"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "true"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
  tolerationSeconds: 0  # no tolerate for criticals
```

ryan: also consider 'warm spares' scaled to 1-2 nodes in each zone with ondemand GPUs to absorb sudden spot losses; costs a bit but reduces cold-start and avoided double-charging from long Terminating nodes. we can autoscale warm-spares down overnight.

sahil: another small win — add a node annotation with last_preempt_ts and expose as metric. we can then smooth scaling decisions in autoscaler webhook to prefer zones with fewer recent preempts.

marta: ok action list I’ll own:
- bump preempt hook TTL to 5m for gpu-spot-nodegroup (quick)
- deploy preempt-prober daemonset with staircase script (this week)
- change autoscaler expander to least-waste and unneededTime=10m (safety)
- add warm-spare ondemand pool in us-west1 zone-b with 2 GPUs (measure cost delta)

kevin: I'll take the autoscaler patch and test in canary cluster.

olivia: I'll own the daemonset + proof-of-concept for checkpoint annotations.

infra-bot: deployed canary autoscaler config to cluster-canary at 2026-03-18T03:20:00Z :rocket:

sahil: nice. once canary looks good let's roll to prod and measure 24h cost delta. also add a Grafana panel for "preemptions per zone" and "avg drain time".

marta: thanks team — will follow up with PRs and dashboards. :thumbsup:
